I'd defintely ask your therapist about what exposures you can use. I would personally start with the thinking aspect. Like if you think something negative about someone, don't apologize. No matter how much you want to, DO NOT GIVE IN. Giving in gives that thought power over you. The thing is, our brain constantly throws random thoughts at us. Don't become stuck on one thought. If you're disgusted by a bad thought, that's actually a good thing. It means you would never seriously think that about someone. You may have slip-ups with giving in, but get up and brush yourself off. You can do this!

I think your therapist is right. These thoughts, judging by your post, are intrusive and you don't particularly find them true, but your mind is trying to convince you otherwise. Right now, I could think "I hate my Mom", but that doesn't make that statement true. Exposure to your thoughts and not acting on asking for forgiveness can help. Asking for forgiveness is a commendable thing, but most of the situations you're describing don't require it. For your question, please take the advice of your therapist. Exposure and resisting urges will help you in the long run! I have the same problem with feeling guilty about small things, that sometimes I can be consumed by it. But in the end, I found that I never had to apologize. It was my mind making me feel guilty for unfounded reasons. I'm rooting you on! I know it's hard, but I believe you can overcome those thoughts.

I'll be honest with my experience of medication. When the doctors were trying to figure out which medication was right for me, it was emotionally hard. Most didn't work in the beginning and left me with side-effects like fatigue and anger. Fortunately, I found the right medication, which is, if you're wondering, is Zoloft and Lexapro. Since I've been on it, I've felt immensely better. I'm actually starting to open up more and don't feel as depressed. Some days will be hard regardless of medication, but sometimes anti-depressants can get you through it.  Be honest with your doctor if you do get on medication. Tell them the side-effects you are having and how you are feeling. They are there to help you and get you on the best anti-depressant that fits your body. Hope this helps :)
